metadata.name: Heart failure (chronic)
metadata.emergency_level: Chronic - but acute/decompensated heart failure and pulmonary oedema are emergencies
metadata.severity: Graded (NYHA I-IV); progressive with significant mortality

overview.short_description: A clinical syndrome in which the heart cannot pump/fill adequately to meet the body's needs, causing breathlessness, fatigue and fluid retention (oedema); classified by ejection fraction (reduced/preserved).
overview.detailed_description: Heart failure is common, disabling and has a poor prognosis if untreated. Diagnosis combines symptoms/signs with a raised natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) and echocardiography (which defines HFrEF vs HFpEF and the cause). Management of HFrEF is highly effective, disease-modifying medical therapy plus device therapy in selected patients; HFpEF management focuses on symptoms, comorbidities and SGLT2 inhibitors. Recognising and treating acute decompensation/pulmonary oedema is critical.
overview.pathophysiology: An initiating insult (ischaemia, hypertension, valve disease, cardiomyopathy) impairs cardiac output; neurohormonal activation (RAAS, sympathetic) initially compensates but drives adverse remodelling, congestion and progressive dysfunction.
overview.etiology: Ischaemic heart disease (common), hypertension, valvular disease, cardiomyopathies, arrhythmias (e.g., AF), alcohol/toxins, high-output states, and others.
overview.natural_history: Chronic and progressive with acute decompensations; modern therapy substantially improves survival and hospitalisation in HFrEF.
overview.prognosis: Serious - comparable to some cancers if untreated; markedly improved by guideline-directed medical therapy and adherence.

prevalence.value: Common, rising with age; affects a significant percentage of the elderly.

mortality.value: High if untreated; a major cause of hospital admission and death.

epidemiology.sex_predominance: HFrEF more common in men; HFpEF more common in older women.

risk_factors.lifestyle: High salt/fluid intake worsens congestion; inactivity.
risk_factors.medications: Some drugs worsen HF (NSAIDs, certain calcium-channel blockers, some diabetes/cancer drugs).
risk_factors.previous_diseases: Coronary disease/MI, hypertension, valve disease, atrial fibrillation, cardiomyopathy, chronic kidney disease.

symptoms.symptom: Acute severe breathlessness at rest, frothy/pink sputum, cannot lie flat (pulmonary oedema)
symptoms.importance: RED FLAG - acute decompensated heart failure

negative_findings.why_important: A normal natriuretic peptide makes heart failure unlikely (high negative predictive value)

negative_findings.finding: No orthopnoea/PND, no raised JVP or oedema, normal ECG

history_questions.question: Are you breathless on exertion, when lying flat, or waking at night gasping?
history_questions.why_ask: Orthopnoea/PND are relatively specific congestive symptoms

history_questions.question: Any ankle swelling, weight gain, and reduced exercise tolerance?
History of heart attack, hypertension, valve disease, AF, or alcohol excess?
Any chest pain, palpitations, or blackouts?

physical_examination.expected_finding: Bibasal crackles; displaced apex; third heart sound (S3); murmurs (valve disease)
Pitting oedema; weight change tracks fluid

physical_examination.examination: Blood pressure, heart rate/rhythm, oxygen saturation

vital_signs.blood_pressure: Variable; low BP indicates poor prognosis/advanced disease
vital_signs.oxygen_saturation: May be reduced in pulmonary oedema
vital_signs.bmi: Variable; cachexia in advanced HF is a poor sign

laboratory_tests.indication: First-line test in suspected heart failure
laboratory_tests.expected_result: Raised in heart failure (higher levels -> more urgent echo)

laboratory_tests.test_name: FBC, U&E, LFTs, glucose/HbA1c, TFTs, iron studies
laboratory_tests.expected_result: Identify contributors (anaemia, renal, thyroid, iron deficiency)

imaging.when_needed: To confirm diagnosis, measure ejection fraction (HFrEF vs HFpEF), and find the cause

ecg.when_needed: In all with suspected heart failure
ecg.findings: Often abnormal (prior MI, LVH, AF, conduction disease); a completely normal ECG makes HF less likely.

other_diagnostic_tests.biopsy: Endomyocardial biopsy only in selected cardiomyopathies
other_diagnostic_tests.cardiac_mri: For cardiomyopathy characterisation in selected cases

diagnostic_criteria.formal_criteria: Symptoms and/or signs of heart failure PLUS objective evidence of cardiac dysfunction. Pathway (NICE NG106/ESC): measure NT-proBNP - if raised, arrange echocardiography and specialist assessment. Classify by LVEF (HFrEF <=40%, HFmrEF 41-49%, HFpEF >=50%) and grade severity by NYHA class.

diagnostic_scores.value: NYHA functional classes I-IV grade symptom severity.

cutoff_values.value: NT-proBNP referral thresholds (NICE): >2000 ng/L urgent (specialist assessment + echo within 2 weeks); 400-2000 ng/L within 6 weeks; <400 ng/L makes HF less likely. LVEF <=40% defines HFrEF.

differential_diagnosis.differences: Airflow obstruction, smoking history, less orthopnoea/oedema, normal NT-proBNP
differential_diagnosis.differential_questions: Is there wheeze and a smoking history rather than orthopnoea/oedema?

differential_diagnosis.disease: Other causes of oedema (venous insufficiency, renal, hepatic, drugs)
differential_diagnosis.differences: No cardiac symptoms/raised JVP; cause-specific features

differential_diagnosis.differential_questions: Are you anaemic or is your thyroid abnormal?

differential_diagnosis.disease: Acute decompensated heart failure / pulmonary oedema
differential_diagnosis.differences: Acute, at rest, frothy sputum, hypoxia
differential_diagnosis.differential_questions: Are you acutely severely breathless at rest, unable to lie flat?

diagnostic_questions.question: Are you severely breathless at rest right now, unable to lie flat, or coughing pink frothy sputum?
diagnostic_questions.target_disease: Acute decompensated heart failure / pulmonary oedema

diagnostic_questions.question: Do you get breathless lying flat or wake at night gasping, with ankle swelling?
diagnostic_questions.interpretation: Orthopnoea/PND + oedema -> supports HF; confirm with NT-proBNP/echo

next_best_question.question: Any acute severe symptoms now, what are the congestive features, and what is the likely cause?
next_best_question.branching_logic: Acute pulmonary oedema -> emergency; chronic -> NT-proBNP then echocardiography, start/refer for guideline-directed therapy

next_best_test.why: Confirms diagnosis, ejection fraction and cause

red_flags.finding: Acute severe breathlessness at rest, unable to lie flat, pink frothy sputum, hypoxia (pulmonary oedema)
red_flags.immediate_action: Emergency - sit up, high-flow oxygen, IV diuretics/nitrates, urgent admission

red_flags.finding: Hypotension/shock, or heart failure with acute coronary syndrome/arrhythmia

red_flags.immediate_action: Urgent specialist assessment and echocardiography (within 2 weeks)

red_flags.finding: Rapid weight gain and worsening congestion

referral_criteria.urgent_referral: Suspected heart failure with very high NT-proBNP (specialist assessment + echo within 2 weeks); acute decompensation (emergency).
referral_criteria.routine_referral: Raised NT-proBNP (400-2000 ng/L) for specialist assessment and echo within 6 weeks; specialist input for HFrEF therapy optimisation and device therapy.

initial_management.supportive_care: Education and self-management (daily weights, fluid/salt advice, recognise decompensation); vaccination; treat the cause and precipitants; multidisciplinary heart-failure team.
initial_management.medications: Canonical schema 1.3 guidance: use treatment_guidance.medication_options and its history-based safety checks. Candidate classes/options (not a prescription): ACE inhibitor/ARB/ARNI; Evidence-based beta-blocker; Mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist; SGLT-2 inhibitor; Loop diuretic. No autonomous selection or dosing is allowed. Source IDs: NICE_NG106_2025.
initial_management.lifestyle_advice: Salt/fluid moderation, daily weights, regular tailored activity/cardiac rehab, smoking cessation, limit alcohol, medication adherence.
initial_management.follow_up: Regular review with up-titration of therapy, renal/electrolyte monitoring, and symptom/congestion assessment; prompt review of decompensation.
initial_management.legacy_medications_pre_v13: HFrEF - guideline-directed medical therapy (the 'four pillars'): ACE inhibitor/ARB or ARNI, beta-blocker, mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist, and SGLT2 inhibitor; loop diuretics for congestion (symptom relief). Consider device therapy (ICD/CRT) and specialist add-ons in selected patients. HFpEF - SGLT2 inhibitor, manage congestion and comorbidities (hypertension, AF, obesity). Correct iron deficiency; avoid HF-worsening drugs (NSAIDs).

patient_education.home_advice: Heart failure means the heart isn't pumping as well as it should, causing breathlessness, tiredness and swelling. Modern medicines greatly improve how you feel and how long you live - take all of them every day, even when well. Weigh yourself regularly: a rapid weight gain or increasing breathlessness/swelling means fluid is building up - contact your team. Get emergency help if you become severely breathless, especially unable to lie flat or coughing pink frothy phlegm.
patient_education.home_advice_ar: قصور القلب يعني أن القلب لا يضخّ كما ينبغي، فيسبّب ضيق النفس والتعب والتورّم. الأدوية الحديثة تُحسّن شعورك وعمرك كثيراً - تناولها كلها يومياً حتى وأنت بخير. زِن نفسك بانتظام: زيادة الوزن السريعة أو ازدياد ضيق النفس/التورّم تعني تراكم السوائل - تواصل مع فريقك. اطلب المساعدة الطارئة إذا صرت شديد ضيق النفس، خاصةً إن عجزت عن الاستلقاء أو خرج بلغم زهري رغوي.
patient_education.prevention: Manage blood pressure, coronary disease and diabetes; healthy lifestyle; adherence to therapy and vaccinations.
patient_education.warning_signs: Rapid weight gain, increasing swelling or breathlessness, breathlessness lying flat, or pink frothy sputum - seek urgent/emergency care.

prevention.vaccination: Influenza and pneumococcal (and COVID-19) vaccination recommended.
prevention.lifestyle: Control of hypertension, coronary disease, diabetes; healthy lifestyle - primary prevention.
prevention.screening: No general screening; case-finding via NT-proBNP in symptomatic patients.

evidence.evidence_level: High - strong trial evidence for guideline-directed therapy in HFrEF and SGLT2 inhibitors in HFpEF.
evidence.guideline_strength: The main diagnosis/test and treatment direction was checked against the current guidance identified by NICE_NG106_2025; see evidence_review for scope and limitations. This does not verify every legacy narrative sentence.
evidence.legacy_guideline_strength_pre_v13: Strong - NICE NG106, ESC heart failure guidelines.

Candidate classes/options (not a prescription): ACE inhibitor/ARB/ARNI; Evidence-based beta-blocker; Mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist; SGLT-2 inhibitor; Loop diuretic. No autonomous selection or dosing is allowed. Source IDs: NICE_NG106_2025.

pregnancy or breastfeeding status when relevant
documented drug allergies and the exact reaction
all prescribed, OTC, herbal and recreational substances

medication_options.when_to_consider: According to ejection-fraction phenotype and specialist/current pathway
medication_options.dose_policy: Dose is not inferred from this KB; use age, weight, renal/hepatic function, pregnancy status and the current local formulary/medicine label.

avoid_if: pregnancy, prior ACE-inhibitor angioedema for ACE inhibitors, bilateral renal artery stenosis, or severe hyperkalaemia
use_caution_if: chronic kidney disease, dehydration, low blood pressure, or potassium-raising medicines
monitoring: creatinine/eGFR, potassium and blood pressure before and after initiation/titration

use_caution_if: asthma/COPD, peripheral vascular disease, diabetes with hypoglycaemia, or acute decompensated heart failure
